summary: The Big Red pierhead light at Holland, Michigan, lit in 1870 or 1873 on the south pier, painted red in 1956, now owned by a local commission.

access.note: Lighthouse Society record: open to the public. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed; south side of the entrance mainly private property with limited public access on foot.

events.note: Wooden beacon on the south pier; LighthouseFriends and the commission's history date the first light to 1870
Year established in the Lighthouse Society's record; the commission's history and LighthouseFriends give 1870
Post light at the outer end of the south pier carried away by the scow Breakaway while entering the harbor; post rebuilt
Lantern carriage and wire rope provided to run the lantern light out to the post
Square pyramidal steel tower replaced the post light on 4 January 1902
Gale on 22 December 1904 damaged the crib beneath the steel tower; light discontinued
Steam fog signal building with quarters for two assistant keepers
Fourth-order Fresnel lens installed in the tower
Square tower erected on the fog-signal building; USLHS gives 1936 as the year the current tower was established
Sandblasted and painted red, earning the name Big Red
Coast Guard announced plans to abandon the light; Coast Guard later kept it as an aesthetic landmark
Holland Harbor Lighthouse Historical Commission formed to save and restore the light
National Register of Historic Places, NRIS 78001509
Fresnel lens moved to the Holland Museum; acrylic lens installed
National Park Service transferred the light to the commission in February 2007

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and the commission's history date the first light to 1870 (wooden beacon on the south pier, first shown December 1870). The Lighthouse Society's record gives 1873 as the year established. The story says the sources differ and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: First light: the record's 1872 (Rowlett) and 1873 (USLHS) against LighthouseFriends and the commission's 1870. The Board's reports 1891-1901 in the corpus do not give a first-lit year for the pierhead light; the 1870s reports are not in the corpus. The story states the disagreement. Appropriation: LighthouseFriends gives $6,000 (15 July 1870); the commission gives $4,000. Not reconciled. Keeper tenure: Van Regenmorter 1870-1907 in the USLHS roster and LighthouseFriends; 1874-1907 in the commission's history. Boshka 1911-1940 (roster, LighthouseFriends) against 1912-1940 (commission). Efficiency flag year: the Bulletin index does not print a year; LighthouseFriends says 1916 for the model-station pennant; the story says so. Breakaway (1890): the Board's 1891 report OCR reads 'Sept<' for the month; the year is 1890 by the fiscal year and LighthouseFriends ('later that year'). OCR page 169 is cited by scan page only; printed page not confirmed. Current tower 1936: USLHS gives 'Tower Construction Material: WOOD' and 'Open to Public: Yes'; LighthouseFriends and the commission describe a 1936 tower on the 1907 fog-signal building without naming its material. The record's 1872 wooden tower (13.0 m) is not confirmed by any source read here. Access: LighthouseFriends' most specific access rules describe summer 2014 (weekdays and Tuesday/Thursday for locals) and must be checked; the commission's page was read for history only. The commission's history also mentions a US Life-Saving Station built beside the keeper's house in 1886 and a 2026 marker that corrects earlier information; neither was checked and neither is used. LighthouseFriends quotes a Coast Guard letter of about 1970; the story uses one short phrase from it. Fog signal: the 1907 date and whistle are from LighthouseFriends and the commission; no Board report in the corpus covers 1907. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the commission's history gives a 34-foot focal height for the 1870 beacon where LighthouseFriends gives 32 feet; both are stated. The founding date 1847 was removed from the opening of 'The place' because no source read for this story dates the settlement to 1847 (LighthouseFriends describes the area's condition in 1847). The Bulletin index entry for Boshka is on PDF page 5 and the Holland range light entry on PDF page 20; LighthouseFriends dates the model-station award to 1916 and the pennant to the following year, and the story says so. The commission's keeper dates differ from the roster for George J. Cornell and Edward Mallette (commission: Cornell 1910-1911, Mallette 1911-1912; roster: Cornell 1910, Mallette 1910-1911); not used in the story. The USLHS record gives the 1936 tower's material as wood and the commission's history does not name it. Location County: OTTAWA in the USLHS record is not used.
